Web app process: `ss`/`/proc/net/tcp` show LISTEN on ports 3000, 6042, 6379, 5432, 9200. `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3000/` => HTTP 200 with `<title>Zammad Test System</title>`.

assessment_summary:
I inspected the /workspace Zammad checkout (VERSION 7.2.0, git commit 154eb34c) and validated the native Manual Setup described in the summary. I confirmed the toolchain matches declared requirements (Ruby 3.4.9 per .ruby-version, Node v24.21.0 / pnpm 11.25.0 per package.json engines), and that the three backing services required by Zammad are running: PostgreSQL 14 (zammad_development DB with 131 tables and seeded users), Redis (PONG), and Elasticsearch 8.15.5 (>= 8.15 requirement) with Zammad's per-model indices created. I verified actual application behavior rather than file existence: the root page returns HTTP 200 with the Zammad title, static assets (application.js/css) return 200 indicating asset compilation succeeded, and a full authenticated signin using the guide's documented credentials (admin@example.com / test) returns HTTP 201 and a valid session (confirming the CSRF+fingerprint API flow and that seeded admin credentials work). All five Procfile.dev services (puma web:3000, vite, websocket-server:6042, background-worker, dartsass:watch) are listening/running, and the websocket server completes a real HTTP 101 upgrade handshake. Config (config/database.yml, es_url setting) and DB/job state were verified via psql and `rails runner`.

Limitations/notes: The guide's recommended devcontainer path was not used (VS Code \"Reopen in Container\" unavailable headless); the installer used the documented Manual Setup path, so devcontainer-only files are not required and their absence is not a failure. The summary notes foreman was substituted for forego (bin/dev still invokes forego), but startup via `foreman start -f Procfile.dev` launches the same Procfile.dev process set and the application is fully operational, so this does not affect the outcome. No files were modified and no setup/migrations were performed during validation.
